profile.text:
SPAKE2 · 1.0.0
RFC 9382 · IRTF Informational
standards-based teaching profile; not an AD DS, Keycloak or browser feature
Distinguish provisioning, candidate derivation, endpoint-local peer confirmation and usable output without implying application authorization.

Standards-based teaching profile; no live implementation or product-support claim

Starting credentials and trust
Both endpoints provisioned with w
Agreed A=server/M and B=client/N roles
Pinned P-256 official vector profile
Immutable synthetic vector-reference fixtures; no runtime cryptography
RFC vector supplies password-equivalent inputs directly; password/PBKDF/MHF mapping is not specified by the vector
Roles, identities, group and transcript framing are pinned; no editable crypto context
Correct inputs and identical profile bindings; both endpoints confirm independently.
Completion means
Each endpoint verifies the peer confirmation and hands its own required confirmation to the transport before its output key is usable in this bounded profile. Local handoff is distinct from remote receipt/verification; a reciprocal sender can finish while its reply is in flight. No application authorization, ticket, cookie or OAuth token is implied.
Transport profile
Abstract ordered public teaching transport; no standardized transport binding claimed

A public recording is not a password checker. Online guessing, endpoint compromise and verifier-record disclosure are different threats. A confirmed PAKE key is not an authorization grant.

Journey
Fields
Cryptographic detail
Compare with augmented SPAKE2+
SPAKE2+ stores (w0,L), not the prover password/w1, at the verifier. Verifier confirms first; prover responds only after verification.
Compare ordinary recording with record disclosure
Public shares and tags are different from a disclosed verifier record. Disclosure enables verifier impersonation and offline guessing; prover impersonation still requires password recovery.
Compare with Kerberos SPAKE
RFC 9588 is a separate Kerberos preauthentication profile that strengthens an AS reply key, not standalone SPAKE2/SPAKE2+ confirmation or an AD DS feature.

Fields
Cryptographic detail
Balanced PAKE foundation
Standalone SPAKE2 uses a shared password-equivalent and explicit A-first confirmation; it is not the Kerberos binding.
Augmented PAKE foundation
Standalone SPAKE2+ gives the verifier w0,L and verifier-first confirmation, not a Kerberos principal key or TGT.
SPAKE versus timestamp
Permitted fallback loses PAKE offline-dictionary protection; any issued TGT is from encrypted timestamp.

Compare password-derived trust with a separate AD DS certificate-based initial-authentication profile. This is not AD DS SPAKE support.
SPAKE with FAST: separate protection
Inspect FAST armor in a separate AD DS profile. RFC 9588 allows SPAKE within FAST, but this SPAKE teaching profile has no armor and this link does not claim AD SPAKE.

performance.method: Three fresh isolated browser contexts per checkout and mode, serial without acceptance workers. Cold means empty browser HTTP/cache/storage, not cold OS filesystem caches. Startup ends at real held-view readiness plus two animation frames. Picker and selection use real Playwright input and clicks; timings include automation round trips. Quantiles from three observations are descriptive, not statistical significance.
performance.causality: Differences in source/standalone bytes and DOM counts are measured. Attribution to catalog size or rendering cost is an inference, not a CPU-profiled cause.
performance.selectionDiagnosticsMethod: Chrome Performance domain counters are sampled immediately before and after real selection, outside its elapsed timing. Nodes includes detached nodes; liveNodesAfter is the current document count. Durations are Chrome seconds, not inferred function costs.
performance.playbackMethod: Replay start measures a real Play click to positive elapsed progress plus two animation frames. A second real picker search must expose the Basic preset while playback remains playing, monotonic and on the same journey. These are interaction latencies, not frame-rate or screen-reader measurements.
